title: Haloumi and Stuffing Salad
subtitle: with Sweet Potato and Rocket
description: It’s the time of year for excitement around holidays, get-togethers and extra-yummy dinners. Our festive dishes are exactly what’s needed to put everyone in a celebratory mood, with amazing flavours and special little touches. So show friends and fam how much you care and have yourselves a merry little meal!

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Preheat the oven to 220C, fan-forced. Line an oven tray with baking paper. Cut the unpeeled sweet potato into 3cm chunks. Thinly slice the onion. Finely chop the rosemary leaves, discarding the stems. Slice the haloumi. Combine 2 tsp red wine vinegar and 1 tsp sugar in a large bowl. Add half the onion and toss to combine. Set aside to pickle.

Roast veggies: Put the sweet potato on the lined tray. Drizzle with 2 tsp olive oil, scatter over half the rosemary and season with salt and pepper. Roast the sweet potato for 12 mins or until starting to soften. Add the remaining onion to the tray, drizzle with 2 tsp olive oil and roast the veggies for a further 6 mins or until the onion is starting to soften.

Toast croutons: Coarsely tear the bread rolls into bite-sized chunks. Add to the tray with the veggies and roast for a further 5 mins or until the veggies are tender and the bread is golden. Set aside to cool slightly.

Cook haloumi: Combine the tomato chutney, remaining rosemary, ½ tsp sugar and 1 tbs water in a bowl. Heat 2 tsp olive oil in a medium frypan over medium-high heat. Cook the haloumi for 2 mins each side or until golden. Add the chutney mixture and cook, turning regularly, for 1 min or until the haloumi is glazed. Remove from the heat.

Serve up: Add the roasted veggies, croutons and rocket to the pickled onion. Drizzle with 2 tsp olive oil, season with salt and pepper and toss to coat. Divide the salad among plates and top with the glazed haloumi. Scatter with the almonds and enjoy!

Did you know?: Haloumi is a brined, slightly springy cheese originally from Cyprus. Traditionally it was made from a mixture of goat and sheep milk, although these days cow's milk is also used. The haloumi we use is made using vegetable rennet, so it's suitable for vegetarians.
